title: Quant runtime backpressure, graceful degradation, and telemetry playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Post-incident initiative to prevent production-wide throughput collapses triggered by quantization fallback and expensive conversion paths. Goals: introduce runtime backpressure for fallback flows, implement graceful degradation policies, and improve telemetry so root causes can be diagnosed without paging on every degradation.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-26 03:12 UTC a subset of hosted inference pools serving quantized model variants experienced a rapid latency and 5xx spike. The spike persisted for ~42 minutes with elevated tail latency and queues building on several inference workers. Customer-facing errors increased by ~4.8% for affected endpoints and internal autoscaling failed to relieve the bottleneck due to synchronous CPU-bound fallback conversions blocking GPU hotpaths.
root_cause: A recently merged optimizer (batching scheduler change) increased peak concurrent requests per worker. Under that peak, a rare opset mismatch fingerprint caused the quantized kernel selector to mark the op unsupported and take the synchronous fallback path. The fallback path performed CPU-bound dequant/convert of large weight blocks while holding a per-request mutex that serialized many concurrent requests, causing head-of-line blocking and downstream request timeouts. Additionally, there was insufficient visibility into fallback rates and no circuit breaker on the synchronous conversion path.
impact: Latent increase in 5xx and latency for hosted API customers serving quantized variants. Short-term revenue impact estimated as low (few customers affected) but high operational noise (on-call escalation, emergency rollbacks). Increased cost due to burst CPU usage on affected hosts and manual mitigations (traffic routing) performed by SREs.
timeline: 2026-02-26 03:12 UTC - Alert: elevated 5xx and tail latency for /v1/generate on region-us-west-2
2026-02-26 03:17 UTC - Initial mitigation: route traffic to compatible non-quant model variants for high-SLO customers
2026-02-26 03:22 UTC - Partial rollback of batching scheduler feature for affected pool applied (hotfix)
2026-02-26 03:30 UTC - A temporary feature-flag disabled the synchronous fallback converter; stability improved but accuracy regressions observed for some prompts
2026-02-26 03:54 UTC - Traffic restored gradually and monitors confirmed recovery; post-incident triage initiated
detection: Automated SLO monitors alerted on 99th percentile latency and a spike in 5xx. On-call SRE correlated pod-level CPU and mutex contention traces using flamegraphs from the incident window. No pre-existing alert for quant-fallback-rate existed.
mitigations_taken: Immediate traffic steering to model variants that do not trigger fallback (per-route routing)
Hotfix: reverted batching scheduler change on affected pools to reduce concurrency pressure
Feature-flagged synchronous converter to prevent blocking hotpath while a safer async path is prepared
long_term_root_cause_mitigation: Introduce per-model and per-pool fallback-rate metrics and SLOs (counts, latency histogram, CPU cost per fallback)
Design and implement a non-blocking async conversion worker pool for fallback paths so GPU hotpath threads are not blocked
Add a circuit breaker that trips when fallback-rate or conversion-latency crosses thresholds; when tripped, route to alternate model variants or return structured fallback responses
Improve op fingerprinting detection to pre-emptively mark and canary unsupported ops during model onboarding
Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent fallbacks and validate that async conversion path maintains latency SLOs

acceptance_criteria: Fallback rate metrics exist and are surfaced in the Console for all quantized models
Async conversion worker pool reduces mutex contention and keeps 99th percentile latency within SLO during synthetic fallbacks at 5x baseline
Circuit breaker trips and routes traffic to alternate variants in canary tests without cascading failures
Runbook updated and on-call run through completed
tests: Synthetic workload that simulates concurrent fallbacks: verify latency & error rates under heavy load
Regression suite to ensure accuracy remains within delta when fallback circuit breaker routes to alternates
Chaos test to randomly inject op-fingerprint mismatches during scale tests
rollout_plan: Merge feature gates behind a runtime flag. Deploy async conversion worker pool in canary region with increased telemetry. Run canary for 48 hours with synthetic fallback load, then gradually promote the change across regions. Enable circuit breaker in canary first and tune thresholds before global enablement.
monitoring_changes: New alerts: quant_fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m for a pool (P1), quant_fallback_cpu_seconds_total spike > 3x baseline (P2)
Dashboard: fallback heatmap, per-model latency vs fallback-rate scatterplot
